text:
A low-carbohydrate intake depletes glycogen stores and shifts metabolism toward fat oxidation and ketogenesis, impairing high-intensity performance while offering therapeutic benefits for weight loss and glycemic control. Effects depend on the degree and duration of restriction and individual activity level. The note is misleading: low carbohydrate intake does not increase muscle glycogen breakdown to compensate—it reduces glycogen availability and training capacity.  
CONFIDENCE: 78
